title: Obligation and Distance
sentences: Families often expect loyalty that was never actually chosen but simply assumed.
A grown child may feel obliged to visit relatives they barely feel close to anymore.
Whereas friendships can end quietly, family ties are rarely allowed to fade the same way.
Admittedly, shared history creates a bond that is difficult to simply walk away from.
Nevertheless, obligation without genuine connection can become a heavy, silent burden.
Distance, whether physical or emotional, is sometimes the only way to protect oneself.
In fact, some people feel closer to relatives once they have moved far away from them.
Expectations inherited from parents are not always suited to the lives their children lead.
A daughter might reject a career her parents wanted, choosing her own path instead.
On the other hand, that choice can cause guilt that lingers for years afterward.
Real family closeness, in the end, must be built rather than simply assumed to exist.
